source.title: Environmental Impact Statement: South Septage Treatment Plant
source.projectLocation: Alabang-Zapote Road, Barangay Pamplona Uno, Las Piñas City

waterbodyContext.reportedRelationship: The EIS describes Zapote River as part of the Parañaque-Las Piñas River System and says it receives water from Bacoor River and Estero Sia Nombre. It describes the river water as estuarial in nature.
waterbodyContext.interpretation: Historical source-named network context only. It does not provide a permitted, georeferenced channel trace or establish exact boundaries for either river.

sourceStatements: The executive summary says that, based on observations and interviews, there were no fish species and other freshwater flora and fauna in the Zapote River.
The main text says fish and other freshwater flora and fauna were less likely in portions of Zapote River and Bacoor River, based on observations and stakeholder interviews.
fishEvidence.interpretation: Qualitative, undated observation/interview statements with no reported fish taxa or reproducible survey design. They are not fish-species records and must not be projected as fish absence or as a current condition.

samplingEvents.sourceInterpretation: The EIS says the measured values were below the then-cited Class C criterion of 5 mg/L.
The EIS reports multiple parameters outside its cited Class C criteria.

historicalWaterQuality.interpretation: Historical water-quality observations only; not current monitoring, a present-day safety advisory, or fishing guidance.

rightsAndUse.decision: Research-only source attribution and minimal factual notes; do not reproduce report prose, tables, maps or figures. Confirm item-specific reuse terms before any public derivative.

coverageDecision.nextAction: Continue seeking dated, station-resolved fish surveys or specimen records and independently permitted channel geometry for Bacoor and Zapote Rivers. Keep household/city-level fishing context separate from waterbody-specific species claims.
